findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There were no paper towels at the handwashing sink in the employee bathroom. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand-sinks are supplied with paper towels to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: A banana stored in the cooler near the tripe sink was observed in a decaying condition. The banana had turned completely black, losing its natural yellow color. Shown to PIC and the banana was discarded. Ensure that food intended for public consumption is always in good condition.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The facility was observed using a plastic grocery bag to store cut sweet potatoes in a prep cooler. Although the sweet potatoes a fried before being served, the practice of storing food items in plastic grocery bags isn’t ideal. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned and sanitized. The potatoes were transferred to an appropriate container to correct the violation. Ensure that foods are stored in food grade products and never in plastic bags.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of both fryers were observed with a significant amount of dried grease debris. PIC mentioned that the facility cleans the baffles manually in the triple sink. Discussed contacting an outside company to service the duct work of the overhead hood system. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: The hand sink in back does not have disposable towels. Towels were provided to the hand sink. Provide a holder for towels at the hand sink in the back and maintain it stocked with hand towels. The violation is considered corrected at this time. Inspector suggests providing a more permanent place for towels so that a supply remains at the hand sink.

Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Inspector observed a container of milk base in the prep cooler reach in section which is dated 10/24/24. This quart of liquid was discarded at time of inspection. Make sure to provide date mark that does not wipe off. Hot dogs and cheese in containers on the top of large prep table in back have labels that allow the date to wipe off. The date is barely visible. Ensure that the date is visible.

(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11 single use items are observed to be stored on the floor in the back storage area and in the front by the hand sink. The items were moved up off of the floor before the inspector left the facility.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17 Hot dogs and cheese open and prepared for battering have no date marking. Items were provided with 7 day date marking tags at time of inspection. Owner states that they use prepared quantities in 3 days. Violation was corrected on sirte.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 & 12 Hand sink shall be supplied with soap and single use towels.

Hand sink in the back does not have soap and single use towels provided to it. Soap and single use towels were provided to the hand sink. Violation was corrected on site.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee recontaminate her hands by washing hands and then using her hands to turn off the faucet. Use a clean barrier to operate faucet handles in order to maintain hands clean.  The employee was stopped and coached immediately. Violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Mixes and batters are made but not date marked. Ube and milk tea are made but not date marked. Date mark items in the facility that are able to support the growth of bacteria. Mixes were made yesterday and ube and milk tea were made Monday. The items were properly date marked at the time of inspection. Develop a habit of proper date marking. Violation is considered corrected at time of inspection.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Utensils for food preparation are observed to be stored in white jars/crocks with handles down. This storage practice leaves the food contact ends exposed to hand contact and potential contamination. Store these items properly protected by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

Observed boxes of single use items stored directly on the floor. Move boxes up off of the floor to properly protect them from potential contamination. 
Single use spoons at the ice cream area are stored in a container with crumbs and debris in the bottom. Clean the holder and maintain container free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: No certified person was present during the inspection. The person present has not even taken the course. The present party did indicate he would be present throughout the day and would be fine taking the CFPM course. The owner arrived within 20 minutes of inspection and began showing progress to the space. 
(A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

Observed no general knowledge on how larger mixing basin and mixing utensil are being washed, rinsed, sanitized. 3 compartment sink is smaller than utensils. Inspector will follow-up on 10/5/22.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

Observed PIC to wash hands correctly, but use no barrier to turn off faucet. Utilize paper towels. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

Observed no CFPM. PIC stated neither owner has obtained it. Food handler verified. PIC stated owners will not pay for her to take. No CFPM's available at facility. Ensure at least TWO. Need for all hours of operation (need at least 1 during operational hours).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Observed no hand washing between glove changes. Observed minimal hand washing. Discussed with manager and employees. Hands should be frequently washed with warm water and soap for 20 seconds and handles of faucet should be turned off with a barrier such as a paper towel. Utilize a hand sink only. If different tasks occur that could contaminate hands, wash hands before donning new gloves. COS.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under ¶¶ 3-301.11(B) and (E). 

Observed ice scoop handle to be immersed in the ice basin. Cease practice. Discussed with employees and PIC. Handles should be placed up right in the ice basin to prevent cross contamination of ready-to-eat foods (ice). COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed no paper towels at the kitchen hand sink. Employee had to bring paper towel to inspector in order to dry hands and turn off the faucet handles. Discussed with PIC and employee’s. Paper towels should be available at all times at the hand sink in order to properly wash hands and turn off the faucets AFTER washing and drying hands (must have a barrier between faucet and clean hands). COS.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

Observed the bleach sanitizer bottle to be too strong - well over 200 ppm. Test strip turned black then immediately turned white - bleached test strip out. Discussed bleach to water ratio in a spray bottle with employee. Discussed that bleach test strips should turn dark purple/black and not turn white again. 50 to 200 ppm - use examples on side of bleach test strip bottles to compare. COS - 200 ppm.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

Observed much of the dry storage to have boxes of food directly on the ground. Cease practice. Boxes should be at least 6 inches off the ground - hinder pests. Ensure boxes are lifted above the floor before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed in-use rags to be on counters. Cease practice. Discussed in-use rag practices with employees. If utilizing a sanitizer bucket with bleach, ensure rags are immersed in bleach when not being utilized. Ensure bleach stays at the concentration of 50 to 200 ppm. If utilizing a spray bottle of bleach, do not use rags. Utilize paper towels and discard. COS.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed multiple areas where single service items were not flipped over to prevent cross contamination. Ensure items are flipped over so food- and lip-contact surfaces are not exposed. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Observed no test strips for the quaternary ammonium. Discussed with PIC. Facility is utilizing both bleach and quaternary ammonium for sanitizer. Bleach test strips available. Ensure both types of test strips are at the facility. Inspector will follow-up on 5/9/22.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no working sanitizer bucket and/or spray bottle in the kitchen area. Discussed issue with multiple employee’s and PIC. A working sanitization method must be available in the kitchen at all times of operation. Change bleach as needed to maintain 50 to 200 ppm. Spray bottle was produced - 200 ppm. Utilize paper towels to clean surfaces with spray bottle of bleach. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas to not be smooth, easily cleanable, and/or non absorbent:
1. The ceiling tiles above the kitchen are black. Change to white ceiling tiles that are not acoustic style before next routine inspection.
2. The storage shelves of the dry storage have duct tape on them and are not sealed/painted. Ensure duct tape is removed (not approved material) and the shelves are painted and/or sealed with a sealant. 

Discussed with PIC. Correct before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Observe the mop to be stored within the mop bucket. Cease practice. Mops should be hung in a manner that allows to air and/or drip dry. Discussed with PIC and employees.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools. 

Observed mop waste water to be within the mop bucket. Cease practice. Mop water should be disposed of within the mop/utility sink after use. Discussed with PIC and employees.
